title: Dental PPO Plans Upgrade Waiting Period Credit for Earlier Coverage on Prior-Level Corrections
content:
Benefit provision, Dental PPO Plans. When a paid line is reprocessed after it was paid at the coinsurance of the plan held before an upgrade (a reprocessed prior-level line), the months credited toward its waiting period follow the person's earlier coverage, and so decide the patient share on such a line.

**Credit.**
- When the plan credits prior coverage month for month and the person (matched by name and date of birth) has a terminated Cascade enrollment in the Prepaid Dental HMO Plans that ended on the day before the Dental PPO enrollment's coverage effective date (a move from the DHMO with no break in coverage): the calendar months from the month that DHMO coverage took effect through the month it ended, both months counted (DHMO coverage always takes effect on the first of a month).
- When the plan credits prior coverage month for month, no such DHMO enrollment exists, and the enrollment shows documented prior coverage months whose prior coverage end date is no more than 63 calendar days before the coverage effective date: those documented months.
- Otherwise: no months.

The months credited shorten the waiting period, never below zero. "The day before the coverage effective date" is the calendar day before it: for coverage effective on the 1st of a month, the last day of the previous month.

**By plan.** Value 1000, Classic 1250, Plus 1500, Premier 2000 and Elite 2500 credit month for month; Preventive 750 credits none. The 63-day figure is the same on every plan.

### Hypothetical cases
| DHMO enrollment | Documented prior coverage | Dental PPO effective | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 January to 31 May, terminated | none | 1 June | 5 months |
| 1 January to 30 April, terminated | none | 1 June | none (did not end the day before) |
| none | 8 months, ended 40 days before | 1 June | 8 months |
| none | 8 months, ended 70 days before | 1 June | none |
